properties.foundation_analysis: The subterranean geology consists of the Lower Carboniferous Gullane and Wardie Shales of the Strathclyde Group, overlain by dense, poorly drained glacial lodgement till perched above the deep gorge of the Water of Leith. The primary structural masonry is premium pale grey-to-buff Craigleith sandstone (quartz-arenite with siliceous and calcareous matrix), celebrated for its low porosity and structural compressive strength. Lime mortar joints consist of hot-mixed calcitic non-hydraulic lime and river sand aggregate. Bedrock gradient and natural groundwater drain northwestward toward the Water of Leith via sub-pavement subterranean cellar drainage systems.

properties.primary_surfacing: Engineered roadway and paved pedestrian curbs
properties.wear_characteristics: Authentic environmental patina and drainage grading

properties.botanical_analysis: To the rear and along the central crescent garden, mature deciduous canopy trees characteristic of the Edinburgh urban landscape: mature Common Beech (*Fagus sylvatica*), Sycamore (*Acer pseudoplatanus*), Wych Elm (*Ulmus glabra*), and Lime trees (*Tilia cordata*). Tree canopies are fully disambiguated from built structures, exhibiting organic, branching leaf mass with textured bark, dappled foliage, and underlying turf borders.

properties.architectural_summary:
Designed by James Gillespie Graham (Moray Feu scheme, 1822–1830), the structure is a Grade A listed neoclassical curved terrace/oval crescent. 
- **Typology & Storeys:** 3-storey, attic, and raised basement residential palace block with advanced multi-bay terminal and central pavilions. 
- **Planar Rectification & Load Bearing:** Facades follow a geometrically true concave arc with plumb vertical ashlar lines. Rusticated ground floors feature V-jointed channel courses. Floor plates, continuous cill courses, entablatures, and coped blocking courses are rigorously level.
- **Roof Geometry:** Sharp, dual-pitched Scottish M-roof profiles and hipped pavilion projections clad in authentic Welsh and West Highland (Easdale/Ballachulish) grey-black slates, punctured by lead-flashed skylights, conical cupolas, and rectilinear ashlar chimney stacks with terracotta cylindrical flues.
- **Fenestration:** Timber sliding sash and case windows (principally 12-pane configurations) set into deep rectangular reveals with continuous stone architraves and classical pedimented/corniced headers at the piano nobile.
